antidotes.why: Letting go cures the clinging mind without removing one's home or work.
Like a lotus leaf in water.

chains.summary: Seeing his own people, Arjuna is overcome and his limbs fail. He drops the bow and sits down in grief. He cannot tell which course is better. Confused about what is right, he asks to be taught.
chains.title: Arjuna's collapse

verses.m: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥

verses.m: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verses.sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥

verses.m: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, letting fall his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥

chains.summary: Attachment comes only where we expect a return. Misery comes through attachment, not through work.
chains.title: Misery comes through attachment, not through work

verses.sa: "Misery comes through attachment, not through work."
Attachment comes only where we expect a return.
not from the fact that we love, but from the fact that we want love in return.

chains.summary: Dwelling on an object breeds attachment. Attachment breeds desire. Desire breeds anger. Anger breeds delusion. Delusion causes loss of memory. Loss of memory ruins judgement. With judgement gone, one is lost.
chains.title: The ladder of fall

verses.m: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
verses.sa: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥

verses.m: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the ruin of understanding; and with understanding ruined, a person is lost.
verses.sa: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥

chains.summary: Hope is a river whose water is wishes and whose waves are craving. Its crocodiles are attachment and its birds are restless thoughts. It uproots the tree of steadiness and its whirlpools are delusion. Its high banks are worry. Those who cross it with a clean mind rejoice.
chains.title: The river called Hope

verses.m: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
verses.sa: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥

depicts.sa: perhaps it is a failure and yet we cannot give it up.

depicts.m: A grown person is freed from his bonds as fruit drops from the tree. But a father, even suffering through his love, never lets go of his child.
depicts.sa: मुच्यते बन्धनात्पुरुषं फलं वृक्षान्प्रमुच्यते / क्लिश्यन्नपि सुतस्नेहैः पिता पुत्रं न मुञ्चति
depicts.why: Shows a parent's holding on named with tenderness.

gloss: Holding on to results, people, things, and a fixed picture is the first link of the Gita's ladder of fall. The Mahabharata expresses it in two syllables, ma-ma.

heals.m: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
heals.sa: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥

heals.m: One who acts offering all actions to the Supreme, giving up attachment, is not touched by wrong, as a lotus leaf is not wet by water.
heals.sa: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः । लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥
heals.why: Gives away the claim on one's work so the work stops clinging.

heals.m: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
heals.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥

heals.m: Two syllables are death; three syllables are the eternal. 'Mama' (mine) in two syllables is death; 'na mama' (not mine) is the eternal.
heals.sa: द्व्यक्षरस्तु भवेन्मृत्युस्त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् / ममेति द्व्यक्षरो मृत्युर्नममेति च शाश्वतम्
heals.why: Locates bondage in the single thought mine.

heals.m: What was, ceases to be; what was not, comes to be. Grief has no power to change this. Why then should anyone grieve?
heals.sa: भूत्वा च न भवत्येतदभूत्वा च भविष्यति / शोके न ह्यस्ति सामर्थ्यं शोचेत स कथं नरः
heals.why: Places loss of position inside the ordinary coming and going of things.

heals.m: There is no eye like knowledge, no discipline like truth, no sorrow like attachment, and no happiness like letting go.
heals.sa: नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः / नास्ति रागसमंदुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम्

heals.m: Gathering the threads of attachment to all of these, he twists them into one cord and ties his mind to my feet. Even-minded, wanting nothing, with no elation, grief or fear in his mind: such a good person lives in my heart as wealth lives in a miser's heart. Saints like you are dear to me; I take a body for no other reason.
heals.sa: सब कै ममता ताग बटोरी। मम पद मनहि बाँध बरि डोरी॥ समदरसी इच्छा कछु नाहीं। हरष सोक भय नहिं मन माहीं ॥ अस सज्जन मम उर बस कैसें। लोभी हृदयँ बसइ धनु जैसें॥ तुम्ह सारिखे संत प्रिय मोरें। धरउँ देह नहिं आन निहोरें ॥
heals.why: Shows scattered attachments gathered, not cut.

heals.m: So, Nidagha, knower of truth, in the dealings of worldly life, let go of whatever is lost, and take up whatever comes.
heals.sa: अतो निदाघ तत्त्वज्ञ व्यवहारेषु संसृतेः । नष्टं नष्टमुपेक्षस्व प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपाहर ॥
heals.why: Shows a lost deal, job or plan is allowed to be over.

hero.m: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
hero.sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥

loci.m: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
loci.sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥

loci.m: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
loci.sa: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥

loci.m: There is no eye like knowledge, no discipline like truth, no sorrow like attachment, and no happiness like letting go.
loci.sa: नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः / नास्ति रागसमंदुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम्

practices.m: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
practices.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
practices.why: Shows loosening the pull of what the mind runs to.

practices.m: Thinking this over, I will not insist out of false affection. I bless you, son; only keep the bond of a mother, and don't forget me.
practices.sa: यह बिचारि नहिं करउँ हठ झूठ सनेहु बढ़ाइ। मानि मातु कर नात बलि सुरति बिसरि जनि जाइ ॥

practices.m: In a vessel full of awakening, filled with the oil of detachment and fitted with the wick of devotion, behold the lamp of knowing. In the hollow darkness of delusion it rises of itself. Make detachment the lower fire-stick and knowledge the upper.
practices.sa: स होवाच । वैराग्यतैलसम्पूर्णे भक्तिवर्तिसमन्विते । प्रबोधपूर्णपात्रे तु ज्ञप्तिदीपं विलोकयेत् ॥ मोहान्धकारे निःसारे उदेति स्वयमेव हि । वैराग्यमरणिं कृत्वा ज्ञानं कृत्वोत्तरारणिम् ॥
practices.why: Shows letting go as the fuel.

practices.m: So, Nidagha, knower of truth, in the dealings of worldly life, let go of whatever is lost, and take up whatever comes.
practices.sa: अतो निदाघ तत्त्वज्ञ व्यवहारेषु संसृतेः । नष्टं नष्टमुपेक्षस्व प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपाहर ॥
practices.why: Shows no second look at what has gone.

practices.sa: Your duty is to afford opportunities and to remove obstacles.

practices.m: Dhritarashtra: 'Everything is always unsettled, and this mind is always unsettled. Wise one, tell me of the state that is free from unrest.' Vidura: 'I see no peace for you apart from learning and discipline, apart from mastering the senses, apart from giving up greed.'
practices.sa: नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्रमिदं मनः / यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते नान्यत्र विद्यातपसो नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात् / नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्यामि तेऽनघ

practices.m: If you cannot do even this, then taking refuge in my yoga and with self restrained, give up the fruit of all actions.
practices.sa: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥
practices.why: Gives up the fruit of all actions.

practices.m: Therefore, always do the work that has to be done, without attachment; by working without attachment a person reaches the highest.
practices.sa: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥

stories.l: Loyalty means staying through the bad season, not only the good.
stories.s: A hunter's poisoned arrow withers the tree where a parrot has always lived. The parrot refuses to leave it. Indra, moved by its loyalty, restores the tree.
stories.t: The parrot who stayed with the withered tree

stories.l: Even the wisest parent breaks a little when a child leaves home; that is love.
stories.s: After the wedding the time comes for Sita to leave Mithila. The palace, even the pet parrots, are in tears. Janaka, known everywhere for his detachment, holds his daughter and loses all composure; his ministers have to remind him it is time.
stories.t: Janaka says goodbye to his daughter

stories.l: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.
stories.s: After telling how Prahlada awakened, Vasishtha faces Rama's challenge: if everything comes by effort, wasn't Prahlada saved by Vishnu's grace? Vasishtha answers that Prahlada earned it himself, that the Self and Vishnu are not two, and that sometimes we wake by our own effort and sometimes by grace reached through devotion. Steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango.
stories.t: Prahlada: effort and grace are not rivals

stories.l: Parents protect children best by letting them go when the time comes.
stories.s: The sage Vishwamitra asks King Dasharath to send the teenage Ram and Lakshman to protect his forest rites from demons. Dasharath, who had his sons late in life, offers land, cows, treasure, even his own life instead. Vasishtha reasons with him, and he finally embraces the boys and hands them over.
